ukmt-smc-2015-02.prompt: What is the sum of all the solutions of the equation $6x=\dfrac{150}{x}$?

ukmt-smc-2015-03.prompt: When Louise had her first car, $50$ litres of petrol cost £40. When she filled up the other day, she noticed that $40$ litres of petrol cost £50. By approximately what percentage has the cost of petrol increased over this time?

ukmt-smc-2015-04.prompt: In the diagram, the smaller circle touches the larger circle and also passes through its centre. What fraction of the area of the larger circle is outside the smaller circle?

ukmt-smc-2015-05.prompt: The integer $n$ is the mean of the three numbers $17$, $23$ and $2n$. What is the sum of the digits of $n$?

ukmt-smc-2015-06.prompt: The numbers $5,6,7,8,9,10$ are to be placed, one in each of the circles in the diagram, so that the sum of the numbers in each pair of touching circles is a prime number. The number $5$ is placed in the top circle. Which number is placed in the shaded circle?

ukmt-smc-2015-07.prompt: Which of the following has the largest value?

ukmt-smc-2015-08.prompt: The diagram shows eight small squares. Six of these squares are to be shaded so that the shaded squares form the net of a cube. In how many different ways can this be done?

ukmt-smc-2015-09.prompt: Four different straight lines are drawn on a flat piece of paper. The number of points where two or more lines intersect is counted. Which of the following could *not* be the number of such points?

ukmt-smc-2015-10.prompt: The positive integer $n$ is between $1$ and $20$. Milly adds up all the integers from $1$ to $n$ inclusive. Billy adds up all the integers from $n+1$ to $20$ inclusive. Their totals are the same. What is the value of $n$?

ukmt-smc-2015-11.prompt: Rahid has a large number of cubic building blocks. Each block has sides of length $4$ cm, $6$ cm or $10$ cm. Rahid makes little towers built from three blocks stacked on top of each other. How many different heights of tower can he make?

ukmt-smc-2015-12.prompt: A circle touches the sides of triangle $PQR$ at the points $S$, $T$ and $U$ as shown. Also $\angle PQR=\alpha^\circ$, $\angle PRQ=\beta^\circ$ and $\angle TSU=\gamma^\circ$. Which of the following gives $\gamma$ in terms of $\alpha$ and $\beta$?

ukmt-smc-2015-13.prompt: The Knave of Hearts tells only the truth on Mondays, Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays. He tells only lies on all the other days. The Knave of Diamonds tells only the truth on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays and Mondays. He tells only lies on all the other days. On one day last week, they both said, “Yesterday I told lies.” On which day of the week was that?

ukmt-smc-2015-14.prompt: The triangle shown has an area of $88$ square units. What is the value of $y$?

ukmt-smc-2015-15.prompt: Two vases are cylindrical in shape. The larger vase has diameter $20$ cm. The smaller vase has diameter $10$ cm and height $16$ cm. The larger vase is partially filled with water. Then the empty smaller vase, with the open end at the top, is slowly pushed down into the water, which flows over its rim. When the smaller vase is pushed right down, it is half full of water. What was the original depth of the water in the larger vase?

ukmt-smc-2015-16.prompt: Fnargs are either red or blue and have $2$, $3$ or $4$ heads. A group of six Fnargs consisting of one of each possible form is made to line up such that no immediate neighbours are the same colour nor have the same number of heads. How many ways are there of lining them up from left to right?

ukmt-smc-2015-17.prompt: The diagram shows eight circles of two different sizes. The circles are arranged in concentric pairs so that the centres form a square. Each larger circle touches one other larger circle and two smaller circles. The larger circles have radius $1$. What is the radius of each smaller circle?

ukmt-smc-2015-18.prompt: What is the largest integer $k$ whose square $k^2$ is a factor of $10!$? [$10!=10\times9\times8\times7\times6\times5\times4\times3\times2\times1$.]

ukmt-smc-2015-19.prompt: Three squares are arranged as shown so that their bases lie on a straight line. Also, the corners $P$, $Q$ and $R$ lie on a straight line. The middle square has sides that are $8$ cm longer than the sides of the smallest square. The largest square has sides of length $50$ cm. There are two possible values for the length (in cm) of the sides of the smallest square. Which of the following are they?

ukmt-smc-2015-20.prompt: A square ink pad has sides of length $1$ cm. It is covered in black ink and carefully placed in the middle of a piece of white paper. The square pad is then rotated $180^\circ$ about one of its corners so that all of the pad remains in contact with the paper throughout the turn. The pad is then removed from the paper. What area of paper, in $\text{cm}^2$, is coloured black?

ukmt-smc-2015-21.prompt: The diagram shows a triangle $XYZ$. The sides $XY$, $YZ$ and $XZ$ have lengths $2$, $3$ and $4$ respectively. The lines $AMB$, $PMQ$ and $SMT$ are drawn parallel to the sides of triangle $XYZ$ so that $AP$, $QS$ and $BT$ are of equal length. What is the length of $AP$?

ukmt-smc-2015-22.prompt: Let $f(x)=x+\sqrt{x^2+1}+\dfrac{1}{x-\sqrt{x^2+1}}$. What is the value of $f(2015)$?

ukmt-smc-2015-23.prompt: Given four different non-zero digits, it is possible to form $24$ different four-digit numbers containing each of these four digits. What is the largest prime factor of the sum of the $24$ numbers?

ukmt-smc-2015-24.prompt: Peter has $25$ cards, each printed with a different integer from $1$ to $25$. He wishes to place $N$ cards in a single row so that the numbers on every adjacent pair of cards have a prime factor in common. What is the largest value of $N$ for which this is possible?

ukmt-smc-2015-25.prompt: A function, defined on the set of positive integers, is such that $f(xy)=f(x)+f(y)$ for all $x$ and $y$. It is known that $f(10)=14$ and $f(40)=20$. What is the value of $f(500)$?
